title_en: Beijing Paiert Medical Technology Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Kehuixin Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over technology development contract
ruling_gist_en: In cases of disputes over bilateral contracts, both parties have mutual obligations to perform. If one party fails to actually perform its own obligation due to the other party's breach, but requests the other party to perform, the people's court should not directly dismiss the claim solely based on the requesting party's non-performance of its own obligation. To achieve the purpose of concluding the contract, the court may, based on the facts of the case, render a judgment ordering both parties to perform their mutual obligations.

full_text_en:
Beijing Paiert Medical Technology Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Kehuixin Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over technology development contract

Ruling Summary

In cases involving bilateral contracts where both parties have reciprocal obligations, and one party, due to the other's breach, has not actually performed its own reciprocal obligation but requests the other party to perform its obligation, the people's court should not directly dismiss the claim solely on the ground that the requesting party has not performed its reciprocal obligation. To achieve the purpose of the contract concluded by both parties, the court may, based on the facts of the case, render a judgment requiring both parties to perform their reciprocal obligations.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2021) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 887

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Beijing Paiert Medical Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: 3rd Floor, Building 1, No. 28 Huoju Street, Science Park, Changping District, Beijing.

Legal representative: Qu Chao, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Libo, male, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Huang Haiming, lawyer of Beijing King & Wood Mallessons Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Shenzhen Kehuixin Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 713, Yanluo Anxin Building, Shanmen Community, Yanluo Street, Bao'an District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Ying, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tan Jianbo, male, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Qihan, lawyer of Beijing V&T Law Firm.

The appellant, Beijing Paiert Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Paiert Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2019) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1716 rendered by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court (hereinafter referred to as the original trial court) on December 15, 2020, in a dispute over a technology development contract with the respondent, Shenzhen Kehuixin Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kehuixin Company). Upon accepting the appeal on April 26, 2021, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held two hearings on June 15, 2021, and September 24, 2021. During the proceedings, the appellant Paiert Company changed its original agent ad litem, Fan Xinmei, a lawyer from Beijing Wuchen Law Firm, to Huang Haiming; the respondent Kehuixin Company changed its original agent ad litem, Li Nan, a patent attorney from Beijing Huicheng Zhidao Intellectual Property Agency (Special General Partnership), to Tan Jianbo. The agent ad litem of the appellant Paiert Company, Liu Libo, participated in both hearings; Fan Xinmei participated in the first hearing, and Huang Haiming participated in the second hearing. The agent ad litem of the respondent Kehuixin Company, Zhang Qihan, participated in both hearings, and Tan Jianbo participated in the second hearing. This case has now been concluded.

Appeal requests of Paiert Company: 1. Set aside the original judgment; 2. Amend the judgment to order Kehuixin Company to transfer the right to apply for a patent for invention titled "Surgical Stapler and Control Method Therefor" with application number 201811480727.9 (hereinafter referred to as the patent application in dispute) to Paiert Company; 3. Amend the judgment to order Kehuixin Company to pay Paiert Company liquidated damages of RMB 6,100; 4. Amend the judgment to order Kehuixin Company to compensate Paiert Company for economic losses of RMB 7,750.24; 5. Amend the judgment to order Kehuixin Company to bear Paiert Company's attorney's fees of RMB 100,000 and notarization fees of RMB 4,212; 6. Order Kehuixin Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and reasons: (1) The original trial court's finding that Paiert Company could not prove that Kehuixin Company failed to pass acceptance was erroneous; it should have examined whether the actually delivered design documents complied with the agreement. In its "Reply to the 'Acceptance Report on Design Documents for the Development of the Stapler Electronic Control System'" (hereinafter referred to as the Reply), Kehuixin Company claimed that it had provided documents in accordance with the agreement, but the "Acceptance Report on Design Documents for the Development of the Stapler Electronic Control System" (hereinafter referred to as the Design Document Acceptance Report) formed by Paiert Company based on the verification and acceptance of the documents provided on February 13, 2019, concluded that "acceptance was not passed." The new document package provided by Kehuixin Company on March 28, 2019, exceeded the deadline agreed in the "Supplemental Agreement on Document Submission and Final Payment for the 'Technology Development Contract'" (hereinafter referred to as the Supplemental Agreement), constituting a breach of contract. Even if Paiert Company accepted it in good faith, it could not complete acceptance before April 14, 2019, as stipulated in the Supplemental Agreement. Kehuixin Company's unilateral assertion in the Reply that it had provided the documents in accordance with the "Technology Development Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the contract in dispute) and its indication that it would no longer perform its contractual obligations constituted anticipatory breach. (2) The original trial court's finding that Paiert Company's claim regarding the ownership of the patent application right in dispute lacked a basis for the right of claim was a misunderstanding of the contract terms. The contract in dispute stipulated the ownership of intellectual property rights, providing that the relevant intellectual property rights would belong to Paiert Company only after all development costs were fully settled, which was intended to secure Kehuixin Company's right to receive compensation. Since the documents delivered by Kehuixin Company failed acceptance, Paiert Company had the right to refuse to pay the final payment and did not constitute a breach of contract. (3) On December 5, 2018, when the contract in dispute was still being performed and Kehuixin Company had not yet delivered any documents and no dispute had arisen regarding contract performance, Kehuixin Company applied for the patent in dispute, maliciously appropriating intellectual property rights that should have belonged to Paiert Company. It cannot be ruled out that Kehuixin Company exploited ambiguous terms in the contract to deliberately cause acceptance failure, thereby achieving the purpose of appropriating intellectual property rights.

Kehuixin Company argued in defense: The original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. The appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed. Facts and reasons: (1) The technology development results under the contract in dispute were merely specific embodiments of the patent application in dispute. (2) The email sent by Kehuixin Company to Paiert Company on October 27, 2017, contained Kehuixin Company's own technical solution (hereinafter referred to as the pre-contract solution). Tan Jianbo, as the inventor, had extensive development experience in the electronic control technology field, had filed a series of patent applications, and had read relevant patent literature. The parties negotiated design specifications and parameters based on the pre-contract solution, formed the "Design Requirements for the Stapler Control System" (hereinafter referred to as the System Design Requirements) attached to the contract in dispute, and formally signed the contract in dispute on November 22, 2017. For the purpose of protecting the pre-contract solution, Kehuixin Company applied for the patent in dispute. (3) The dispute between the parties over the design documents resulted from differing understandings of the contract terms and did not involve a breach of contract. Kehuixin Company first submitted documents on January 23, 2019. Paiert Company immediately inspected the documents and requested PCB process requirements, but raised no other objections thereafter, indicating its implicit acceptance that the documents submitted by Kehuixin Company were compliant. In fact, the design documents submitted by Kehuixin Company complied with the contract in dispute. (4) The contract in dispute stipulated that the relevant intellectual property rights would belong to Paiert Company only after all development costs were fully settled, and before that, they belonged to Kehuixin Company. After receiving the documents, Paiert Company unilaterally refused to pay the final payment on the ground that the design documents failed acceptance, constituting a fundamental breach of contract and waiving its right to claim intellectual property rights.

Paiert Company filed a lawsuit with the original trial court, which accepted the case on November 11, 2019. Paiert Company's claims at first instance: 1. Order Kehuixin Company to continue performing its obligations under the contract in dispute, including but not limited to submitting design documents for the stapler electronic control system compliant with the System Design Requirements, source code for the developed system, and eliminating restrictions on program burning, to be verified by Paiert Company to confirm that the design documents meet the functional requirements of the contract in dispute and its attachments; 2. Confirm that the right to apply for the patent in dispute belongs to Paiert Company; 3. Order Kehuixin Company to compensate Paiert Company for losses caused by its breach, i.e., additional sample manufacturing costs of RMB 7,750.24; 4. Order Kehuixin Company to pay liquidated damages of RMB 6,100; 5. Order Kehuixin Company to bear attorney's fees of RMB 100,000 and notarization fees of RMB 4,212; 6. Order Kehuixin Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Kehuixin Company argued in defense at first instance: (1) Paiert Company conducted acceptance based on product development standards, exceeding the scope of development agreed in the contract. Kehuixin Company completed the technical development of the stapler electronic control part in accordance with the contract in dispute and the Supplemental Agreement, submitted all design documents as agreed, and fully performed its contractual obligations. After implicitly accepting the documents as compliant, Paiert Company refused to make payment, constituting a fundamental breach of contract, and the contract between the parties was terminated. Therefore, the contract in dispute lacks a basis for continued performance. (2) The technical solution of the patent application in dispute was independently developed by Kehuixin Company. The contract in dispute only required intellectual property protection for Paiert Company's documents and did not restrict or stipulate Kehuixin Company's filing of patent applications. (3) Kehuixin Company had already performed its contractual obligations. Paiert Company's claims for liquidated damages and compensation for losses lacked factual basis; its claims for attorney's fees and notarization fees should also not be supported.

Facts found by the original trial court:

On November 22, 2017, the parties signed the contract in dispute, with the System Design Requirements as an attachment. The contracting party (Party A) was Paiert Company, and the developer (Party B) was Kehuixin Company. The project name was "Development of Stapler Electronic Control System." The main contents of the contract were as follows: 1. Regarding the subject matter of the contract, the technical content, design requirements, and indicator parameters were detailed in the contract attachment; Kehuixin Company was only responsible for the pure electronic control part, while other parts, including but not limited to structure and mechanics, were to be developed by Paiert Company itself. For indicators involving the coordination of structure and electronics, such as transmission displacement control accuracy, the parties were to jointly negotiate solutions. 2. Regarding design documents, they included design schematics, PCB layout, PCB engineering files, BOM list, embedded software, and design description; within three months after delivering the above documents, Kehuixin Company was to provide remote professional assistance to Paiert Company in completing the electronic control system acceptance and compiling other documents required for product development. 3. Regarding development cycle and technical cooperation, Kehuixin Company was to provide necessary technical support within six months after delivering the documents mentioned in item 2 to assist in completing EMC certification and patent applications. 4. Regarding development funding and payment or settlement method, the total development funding was RMB 75,000 (including tax), payable in three installments of 40%, 40%, and 20%. After Kehuixin Company delivered all design documents and auxiliary documents specified in item 2 of the contract in dispute and Paiert Company accepted them as compliant, Paiert Company was to pay RMB 15,000. 5. Regarding intellectual property rights, the deliverables arising from the performance of the contract [including but not limited to consulting reports, licensed software as configuration documents for the subject matter of the contract in dispute, submitted documents, and development results (including source code)] and related intellectual property rights were to belong to Paiert Company only after all development costs were fully settled; before that, they belonged to Kehuixin Company. 6. Regarding the allocation of risk and liability, if Kehuixin Company violated Articles 1, 2, or 3 of the contract, it should bear liability for breach of contract, with liquidated damages capped at 10% of the amount paid. If Kehuixin Company's breach caused the project to fail, Kehuixin Company should refund the development costs paid; if Paiert Company failed to pay the agreed funding for more than two months, Paiert Company must pay the overdue amount and also pay liquidated damages equal to 10% of the contract amount, and Kehuixin Company had the right to terminate the contract; if Kehuixin Company used Paiert Company's original intellectual property rights or intellectual property rights and technologies or works belonging to Paiert Company newly developed or created under the contract beyond the scope permitted by the contract, Kehuixin Company must bear liability for breach of contract. 7. Regarding dispute resolution, any disputes arising during the performance of the contract should be resolved through negotiation between the parties. The attachment System Design Requirements further stipulated the functional modules for the subject matter of the contract, the "Stapler Control System," including schematic design, PCB, soldering and debugging, software design, etc.

On December 5, 2018, Kehuixin Company filed an application for the patent in dispute with the China National Intellectual Property Administration.

On January 11, 2019, Paiert Company sent the "Acceptance Report for the PE Project Electronic Control System" to Kehuixin Company via email. The report concluded that the acceptance was granted with concessions, allowing entry into the next stage of document acceptance.

During the performance of the contract, the parties also signed the Supplemental Agreement, with Paiert Company signing on January 21, 2019, and Kehuixin Company signing on January 19, 2019. The main contents of the Supplemental Agreement were as follows: Kehuixin Company was to provide design documents by January 24, 2019, and complete improvement and optimization of the subsequent 13 items and update the design documents by March 14, 2019; after receiving the design documents from Kehuixin Company, Paiert Company was to use them for sample manufacturing; the PCB could be adjusted according to Paiert Company's needs, but the PCBA functions for the same firmware version were to be identical; Paiert Company must complete document acceptance by April 14, 2019, failing which the documents would be deemed accepted; after Kehuixin Company provided the documents meeting the conditions in items 1 and 2 and Paiert Company accepted them as compliant, Paiert Company must pay the final payment of RMB 15,000 by May 14, 2019; if payment was overdue, in addition to paying the final payment, Paiert Company must pay a late fee calculated at 1% of the total contract amount per day of delay.

On January 23, 2019, Kehuixin Company sent a document package to Paiert Company via email, mainly including: schematics and PCB files for the battery and control board; source code for the battery and control board; bills of materials for electronic components of the battery and control board; and control board design description. On February 13, 2019, and March 28, 2019, Kehuixin Company sent updated document packages to Paiert Company via email.

On April 1, 2019, Paiert Company issued the Design Document Acceptance Report to Kehuixin Company, concluding that the design documents did not meet the requirements of the contract in dispute and its attachments, and verification failed; the content described in the design description did not meet the requirements for product manufacturing and debugging, and verification failed; the actual sample board tested had significant dimensional deviations and could not be assembled, and functional performance could not be verified accordingly, resulting in verification failure. In summary, the design documents submitted by Kehuixin Company failed acceptance.

In response to the above Design Document Acceptance Report, Kehuixin Company sent the Reply to Paiert Company via email on April 3, 2019, mainly stating that Kehuixin Company had performed its obligations under the contract in dispute and the Supplemental Agreement, and that Paiert Company's conclusion of acceptance failure exceeded the contract scope. Kehuixin Company urged Paiert Company to complete document acceptance by April 14, 2019, as per the Supplemental Agreement. On April 10, 2019, Kehuixin Company sent a paper version of the Reply via SF Express to Paiert Company employee Liu Libo, which was refused; it was then forwarded to Paiert Company employee Bai Yuling via the SF Express ordering system, also refused. On April 11, 2019, Kehuixin Company sent the Reply via EMS, which showed it was signed for on April 15, 2019.

On July 17, 2019, Kehuixin Company issued a notice of rescission to Paiert Company, stating that because Paiert Company failed to pay the final payment of RMB 15,000 by May 14, 2019, as agreed in the contract, and despite multiple reminders from Kehuixin Company, Paiert Company had persistently refused to sign for relevant documents and refused to make payment, constituting a fundamental breach of contract. Kehuixin Company sent the notice to Paiert Company via email on July 19, 2019, stating that the contract was terminated as of the date the email was received.

To prove that the technical elements and sources of the technical solution of the patent application in dispute were derived from the performance of the contract in dispute, Paiert Company submitted to the original trial court two notarized certificates, (2019) Jing Chang'an Nei Jing Zheng Zi Nos. 63470 and 63471, which preserved email correspondence and WeChat chat records between Paiert Company's employee Chen Xiaoqiang and Kehuixin Company's contact person regarding the project development.

To prove its various losses and reasonable expenses, Paiert Company submitted to the original trial court a quotation for "50 sets of stapler control system samples," an invoice for "sample manufacturing costs," showing an amount of RMB 7,750.24; the entrustment contract, payment receipt, and attorney's fee invoice showing an amount of RMB 100,000; and a notarization fee invoice showing an amount of RMB 4,212.

The original trial court held that the contract in dispute, its attachments, and the Supplemental Agreement were all the true intentions of the parties, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and were valid contracts to be performed by both parties in accordance with their terms. In this case, Paiert Company alleged that Kehuixin Company had committed two breaches: first, privately applying for a patent for the technology in the project; second, the design documents submitted by Kehuixin Company failed acceptance.

First, the cause of action in this case is a dispute over a computer software development contract. According to Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, claims based on contractual rights are typically for continued performance, payment of liquidated damages, or compensation for losses. The issue of ownership of the patent application right in dispute was not clearly stipulated in the contract in dispute; therefore, Paiert Company's claim lacked a basis for the right of claim. Even if, according to the contract in dispute, the technical solution of the patent application in dispute might involve "deliverables arising from the performance of this contract," the clause clearly stated that "the relevant intellectual property rights shall belong to Party A only after all development costs are fully settled, and before that, they shall belong to Party B." Therefore, in the absence of evidence that Paiert Company had fully settled all development costs, its claim could not be established.

Second, regarding the system developed by Paierte Company, Chengxin Company first issued an acceptance report on January 11, 2019, and then issued an acceptance report on April 1, 2019, indicating that the design documents did not pass acceptance. Chengxin Company replied on April 3, 2019, pointing out that Paierte Company's acceptance exceeded the scope of the contract and urged Paierte Company to proceed with acceptance. According to the principles of the Contract Law of the PRC and the agreement in Article 9 of the contract in question, the parties should resolve through negotiation whether the design documents submitted by Chengxin Company complied with the agreement and whether acceptance should be approved. Chengxin Company communicated with Paierte Company in a timely manner and responded to and explained the issues in the design document acceptance report in its reply. However, after receiving the reply, Paierte Company did not engage in further communication with Chengxin Company, resulting in a lack of communication and negotiation between the parties on the design documents, and the issue remained unresolved. Therefore, the evidence submitted by Paierte Company is insufficient to prove that the failure of the design documents submitted by Chengxin Company to pass acceptance constitutes a breach of contract under the contract in question. Paierte Company's claim for liquidated damages against Chengxin Company cannot be sustained, and the court of first instance did not support it. Since Paierte Company failed to further negotiate with Chengxin Company regarding the reply and refused to pay the balance, Chengxin Company's letter to Paierte Company rescinding the contract in question complies with paragraph (3) of Article 94 of the Contract Law of the PRC. Therefore, the contract in question was rescinded when Chengxin Company's rescission notice was served on Paierte Company, and the court of first instance confirmed this. Consequently, Paierte Company's claim for specific performance of the contract also has no basis, and the court of first instance did not support it.

As for Paierte Company's claims for additional sample preparation fees, attorney's fees, notarization fees, and other costs, since it has been determined that Chengxin Company did not breach the contract, these claims by Paierte Company also cannot be sustained, and the court of first instance did not support them.

Based on this, the court of first instance, in accordance with paragraph (3) of Article 94 of the Contract Law of the PRC and paragraph 1 of Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (revised in 2017), rendered Civil Judgment (2019) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1716 on December 15, 2020, dismissing all claims of Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. The court acceptance fee of RMB 2,662 for the first instance was borne by Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd.

During the second instance of this court, Paierte Company submitted the following new evidence: 1. A utility model patent document with patent number 201822038269.5, titled "A Surgical Stapler," intended to prove that during the performance period of the contract in question, Chengxin Company filed the above patent application on December 5, 2018, and the patent inventor was Tan Jianbo, which violated the contract terms and constituted a material breach. 2. Emails between Paierte Company's employee Liu Libo and a third party on October 20, 2017, regarding specific indicator parameters for the system design requirements in the contract in question, and the Notarial Certificate (2021) Jing Chang An Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 39001 (hereinafter referred to as Notarial Certificate No. 39001) notarizing these emails, intended to prove that before the contract was signed, earlier than the time shown in the emails submitted by Chengxin Company, Paierte Company had already proposed the system design requirements. 3. Emails sent by Chengxin Company's Tan Jianbo to Paierte Company on October 26, October 27, and November 1, 2017, regarding the quotation for stapler development, and a video of the email login process, intended to prove that Chengxin Company's quotation was a response to Paierte Company's design needs and that before quoting, Chengxin Company recognized requirements such as sample acceptance and submission of design documents. 4. Notarial Certificate (2021) Jing Chang An Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 39000, intended to prove that the materials delivered by Chengxin Company did not meet the acceptance standards. 5. Notarial Certificate (2021) Jing Chang An Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 38999 (hereinafter referred to as Notarial Certificate No. 38999), intended to prove that before signing the contract in question with Chengxin Company, Paierte Company had already communicated with multiple third parties regarding the electric stapler solution. 6. Paierte Company's 2016 Coremail email renewal contract, intended to prove that Paierte Company's email service was provided by a third party, and the email content is objective and true.

Chengxin Company's opinion on the evidence was: It acknowledged the authenticity of Evidence 1; it did not acknowledge the authenticity of Evidence 2 and 3; it acknowledged the authenticity and legality of Evidence 4, 5, and 6 but did not acknowledge their relevance to this case; it argued that the emails in Evidence 2 regarding Liu Libo could not be ruled out as being fabricated from a technical perspective, were not corroborated by other evidence in content, and could not prove that Paierte Company provided the system design requirements to Chengxin Company or that there was any technical suggestion to Chengxin Company's technical solution.

Upon review, this court made the following determinations regarding the authenticity, legality, relevance, and probative value of the above evidence: Paierte Company submitted the originals of Notarial Certificates (2021) Jing Chang An Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 38999, 39000, and 39001. Taking into account Chengxin Company's opinion on the evidence, this court confirms the authenticity of Evidence 1, 4-6; regarding the authenticity of Evidence 2, which includes the system design requirements sent by Paierte Company on October 20, 2017, Evidence 6 can prove that Paierte Company's email system was serviced by a third party and that the above emails were preserved through notarization. In the absence of contrary evidence, the authenticity of Notarial Certificate No. 39001 and the above emails can be determined; regarding Evidence 3, this court will conduct a comprehensive analysis to determine whether the design documents submitted by Chengxin Company complied with the agreement, taking into account other evidence and facts in the case.

Paierte Company argued that the court of first instance omitted to investigate the relevant content of the supplemental agreement. Chengxin Company had no objection to the facts found by the original judgment. Upon review, this court finds that the original judgment found the main content of the supplemental agreement, and Paierte Company's assertion that the original judgment omitted relevant content cannot be sustained.

The facts found by the court of first instance are supported by evidence, and this court confirms them.

This court also finds the following:

(I) Facts related to the patent application in question

The description of the patent application in question states: The technical problem to be solved by the present invention is to provide a surgical stapler and a control method thereof, enabling precise positioning. The beneficial effect of the present invention is that an RFID reader can read the specification information of the jaws, and the controller can control the drive transmission mechanism to drive the jaws to move according to the specification information of the jaws, allowing for precise control of the jaw movement; when the specification information of the jaws is different, the required movement stroke is also different; the surgical stapler of the present invention is applicable to jaws of different specifications; by comparing the actual pulse count and the theoretical pulse count of the encoder, it can be determined whether the jaws have moved to the correct position, enabling precise positioning of the jaws during surgery; the key concept of the present invention lies in providing an RFID reader to read the specification information of the jaws, and the controller can control the drive member to drive the transmission mechanism to move the jaws according to the specification information of the jaws, allowing for precise control of the jaw movement.

(II) Facts related to the contract in question and its performance

The contract in question includes a production agreement clause: If the contract content is successfully developed and passes Paierte Company's verification, Paierte Company shall entrust Chengxin Company with the production of components based on actual needs; before each batch of production is entrusted, the parties must also sign a batch procurement agreement stipulating the entrusted production quantity, total price, and delivery period.

The system design requirements attached to the contract in question include columns such as "Design Requirements" and "Output Products and Documents." The design requirements for the software design include: 1. RFID identification, reading device and tag are small in size, with a reading sensitivity of 100%; output file includes information source code. 2. Motor forward and reverse rotation and push stroke control, with the accuracy of the push stroke for different types of jaws being the set value plus or minus 0.3mm; output file includes source code (including code explanations).

The design document acceptance report issued by Paierte Company includes the following content: Based on the contract in question and its attachments, and in conjunction with the acceptance specifications for the electronic control components and system, verification of the design documents is carried out; the materials not provided by Chengxin Company as agreed include: RFID module PCB layout, schematic diagram, electronic BOM list, source code, etc.; issues with the materials already provided by Chengxin Company include: the source code was not provided in its complete form as required by the contract, along with corresponding code explanations, etc.

Chengxin Company's reply to Paierte Company includes the following content: Article 2 of the contract in question clearly defines the content of the design documents, and multiple places in the contract and its attachments clearly state that the attachments are the basis for technical development, not a list of documents to be submitted. In response to Paierte Company's request for the delivery of complete source code and explanations, the above reply stated: "The contract does not have this excessive requirement."

(III) Other relevant facts

Notarial Certificate No. 38999 preserved evidence of certain content in the corporate email accounts of Paierte Company employees Liu Libo and Bai Yuling. The emails show: In October 2017, Paierte Company engaged in contract negotiations with Huaruan Huisi (Beijing) IOT Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huisi Company). The parties drafted a contract with the subject matter being a stapler control system, and the contract price was RMB 88,000. This contract did not have a production agreement clause; the content of the attachments on which the project development was based was identical to the attachments of the contract in question; the intellectual property clause of this contract was the same as that of the contract in question, namely "The deliverables generated from the execution of this contract (including but not limited to consultation reports, licensed software, configuration documents that are the subject of this contract, submitted documents, and development results (including source code)) and related intellectual property rights are considered commission work, and their ownership and related rights and interests belong to Paierte Company."

Notarial Certificate No. 39001 preserved evidence of certain content in Liu Libo's corporate email account. The emails show: In August 2017, Paierte Company internally communicated on market demand, product functions, mechanical design, circuit design requirements, etc., for an electric endoscopic stapler. On October 20, 2017, during internal communication on the contract content with Huisi Company, Paierte Company formulated system design requirements, which were essentially identical to the attachments of the contract in question.

The contract document negotiated with Huisi Company mentioned above was never finally signed.

During the period of the email correspondence preserved through the above notarization, Paierte Company's corporate email service was provided by a third party, Beijing Chengxun Tianxia Information Technology Co., Ltd.

Paierte Company was established in September 2002, and its business scope includes the production of staplers, skin staplers, clip staplers, purse-string staplers, and Class II medical devices including OO-6809 tubular staplers.

During the second instance proceedings, Paierte Company clearly stated that it was abandoning the first claim from the first instance (i.e., requesting Chengxin Company to continue delivering technical materials and source code for Paierte Company to verify, etc.); at the same time, it stated that since the patent application in question was filed in the name of Chengxin Company, confirming the ownership of the patent application right necessarily involves requesting Chengxin Company to transfer the patent application right to it; regarding the contract balance, Paierte Company expressed its willingness to pay the remaining amount and actually paid it to Chengxin Company's account, but Chengxin Company, believing the contract had been rescinded, returned the funds.

Regarding whether the technical solution involved in the patent application in question is a development result under the contract in question, Chengxin Company, in its submissions at the first instance and during the second instance before this court on June 23, 2021, both confirmed: the main content claimed for protection in the patent application in question is precisely the circuit part that Chengxin Company was responsible for developing as agreed in the contract in question, but argued that the technical solution was independently developed by Chengxin Company. In the second inquiry conducted by this court with the parties, Chengxin Company denied that the technical solution involved in the patent application was a development result under the contract in question, claiming it was a pre-contract solution of Chengxin Company. On this issue, Tan Jianbo, the inventor named in the patent application document, appeared as Chengxin Company's authorized litigation representative in the second inquiry and made the following statement: Achieving an accuracy of 0.3mm was a design indicator; there are many ways to achieve this accuracy; the "how" is the method. When this court inquired which solution was delivered to Paierte Company under the contract in question, Tan Jianbo replied that it was the solution provided in Claim 6 of the patent application.

Opinion of the Court: The signing and performance of the contract in question and the supplemental agreement primarily occurred before January 1, 2021. This case should be governed by the Contract Law of the PRC. Regarding the nature of the legal relationship between Paierte Company and Chengxin Company, Chengxin Company argued that the actual relationship was one of cooperation, that the development fee agreed upon in the contract in question was too low, and that the parties had agreed that Chengxin Company would recover its development costs through agency production. In this regard, the nature of the rights and obligations between the parties should be determined by the main content agreed upon in the contract in question. Although the contract in question includes a "production agreement" clause, in terms of its content, it is an arrangement for a future contract between the parties, constituting a preliminary contract clause and does not form part of the rights and obligations of the parties within the contract in question. From the contractual provisions regarding "providing remote professional assistance to Party A for the completion of the electronic control system acceptance and the compilation of other documents required for product development within three months after delivery of the documents" and "ownership of deliverables (including but not limited to consultation reports, licensed software, configuration documents that are the subject of this contract, submitted documents, and development results (including source code)) and related intellectual property rights generated from the execution of this contract shall belong to Party A after the development fee is settled, and shall belong to Party A before that," it is clear that Paierte Company's contractual purpose is to obtain and master the development results. The primary rights and obligations between the parties constitute a commissioned development relationship, not a cooperative relationship. Furthermore, based on the evidence submitted by Paierte Company, it is evident that it also engaged in contract negotiations with a third party, Huisi Company, for the development project in question. Although the contract text formed during those negotiations was never finally signed, it can serve as a reference for the market cost of the project development. The development fee stipulated in the above contract text was RMB 88,000, and the contract did not include an agency production clause. Therefore, Chengxin Company's claim that it would amortize research and development costs through agency production lacks evidentiary support. The contract in question is a technical development contract, which includes the content of computer software development. This case is a dispute over a technical development contract. The contract in question and the supplemental agreement are the true intentions of both parties and do not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations; therefore, they should be valid. Both parties should exercise their rights and perform their obligations in accordance with the contract. Although Paierte Company no longer insisted on the first-instance claim in the second instance for Chengxin Company to deliver design materials and conduct verification, it still insists on obtaining the patent application right in question. Its true intention is to request Chengxin Company to continue performing the part of the contract in question regarding the delivery of the intellectual property rights of the development results. Based on the parties' respective claims and defenses, the issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: the ownership of the patent application right in question and whether Paierte Company has the right to demand that Chengxin Company bear the alleged liability for breach of contract.

(I) Regarding the ownership of the patent application right in question

1. Regarding the contractual provisions for intellectual property ownership under the contract in question

According to the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 339 of the Contract Law of the PRC, for inventions and creations made during commissioned development, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the right to apply for a patent belongs to the research and developer; if the research and developer obtains the patent right, the commissioning party may exploit the patent for free. In accordance with the provisions of the contract in question regarding document delivery, acceptance, and intellectual property ownership, after Chengxin Company delivers the design documents and auxiliary materials and Paierte Company accepts them as qualified, Paierte Company pays the final contract payment of RMB 15,000; after all development costs are settled, the deliverables and intellectual property rights, including source code, belong to Paierte Company; before settlement, they belong to Chengxin Company. At the same time, the contract in question contains a special provision regarding patent applications: (Chengxin Company) shall provide necessary technical support within six months of delivering the design documents to assist in completing the patent application. Taking the above provisions together, it can be seen that the contract in question stipulates the ownership of the right to apply for a patent for the development results. According to the agreed content, before the development costs are settled, the right to apply for a patent for the development results belongs to Chengxin Company. After settlement, Chengxin Company provides technical support for Paierte Company to file the patent application. Accordingly, whether Paierte Company has the right to request confirmation of the patent application right in question and to demand that Chengxin Company transfer the patent application right to it in this case mainly depends on whether the technology involved in the patent application in question is a development result under the contract in question and whether the condition for settlement of the development costs has been fulfilled.

2. Regarding whether the technology involved in the patent application in question is a development result under the contract in question

Determining this issue requires examining, based on the evidence provided by the parties and their statements during the proceedings, whether the conception and development of the technical solution for the patent application in question originated from the contract in question, and whether the technical problems solved by the patent application in question and the technical means employed are substantively the same as the relevant development content of the contract in question, and conducting a comprehensive analysis to determine whether the commissioned party actually conducted the technical development based on the contract in question. From the content of Chengxin Company's statements during the first and second instances, in its submissions at the first instance and during the second instance filed on June 23, 2021, Chengxin Company both confirmed that the main content claimed for protection in the patent application in question is precisely the circuit part that Chengxin Company was responsible for developing as agreed in the contract in question, effectively acknowledging the fact that the technical solution of the patent application in question is a development result. Subsequently, in the second inquiry, Chengxin Company denied this fact. However, when this court inquired which solution Chengxin Company delivered to Paierte Company, the inventor Tan Jianbo replied that it was the solution adopted by Claim 6 of the patent application. Taking into consideration Chengxin Company's statements above, and considering the following factors, this court determines that the technical solution of the patent application in question was developed by Chengxin Company based on the technical requirements agreed upon in the contract in question, and constitutes a development result under the contract in question that should be delivered to Paierte Company:

First, from the content of the technical solution of the patent application in question. According to the description of the patent application in question, the patent aims to provide a surgical stapler suitable for different specifications of jaws and capable of achieving precise positioning, and a control method therefor. To this end, the patent application adopts an RFID reader to read jaw specification information, and based on that information controls a driving member to drive a transmission device to move the jaws; by comparing the actual number of pulses of the encoder with the theoretical number of pulses, it is determined whether the jaw has moved into position, thereby achieving precise positioning of the jaw. This is consistent with the description in the system design requirements, which served as the basis for development under the contract, in the "software design part" requiring that "the RFID identification reading device and tag be small in size, with a reading sensitivity of 100%" and "advance stroke control: ... the accuracy of the advance stroke for different jaw models is: set value ±0.3 mm". As for controlling the jaw movement stroke by obtaining and comparing the theoretical pulse number and the actual pulse number, this is a specific way to achieve the control accuracy required by the system design requirements. Accordingly, it can be determined that the technical solution of the patent application in question and the content recorded in the system design requirements both control the stroke by reading jaw specification information via an RFID reader, thereby achieving precise positioning of the jaws; both use the same technical means to solve the same technical problem.

Second, from the business matters of the parties. KeHuixin Company stated during the second instance the conception and development process of the technical solution of the patent application in question, but did not provide evidence to prove that it conducted related technical development for other needs; Inventor Tan Jianbo, although having development experience in the field of electronic control technology, had not previously carried out development work in the medical device field, and did not provide evidence to prove its claimed process of independent conception and development. In contrast, Paierte Company, as an enterprise engaged in the medical device business, with its business scope including the production of various types of staplers, submitted evidence such as Notarization No. 39001, which can prove that it carried out preliminary work such as market research and needs design for laparoscopic staplers, and engaged in contract negotiations with other companies for the same development project.

Third, from the defenses of KeHuixin Company. After Paierte Company submitted Notarization No. 39001, KeHuixin Company further argued that the technology of the patent application in question was its pre-contract proposal. Its main evidence was that an email sent to Paierte Company on October 27, 2017, contained the system design requirements. However, Notarization No. 39001 can prove that as early as October 20, 2017, the same system design requirements already appeared in Paierte Company's internal emails. Therefore, the evidence on record cannot prove that the system design requirements were first proposed by KeHuixin Company; the claim by KeHuixin Company that the system design requirements were its pre-contract proposal cannot be established. Furthermore, even if, as KeHuixin Company claims, the system design requirements were first proposed by Tan Jianbo, and the technical solution of the patent application in question was independently conceived and developed by KeHuixin Company, after the parties signed the contract, the system design requirements became part of the contract in question and the basis for KeHuixin Company's development. In a technology commissioned development contract, fulfilling the development tasks using one's own experience and technology is one of the developer's main contractual obligations. Where the contract clearly stipulates the ownership of intellectual property rights, including patent application rights, the fact that KeHuixin Company independently completed the development does not constitute a defense that it should enjoy the patent application right.

3. Whether the conditions for delivery of intellectual property rights in the development results have been satisfied

When Paierte Company filed this lawsuit, it had not yet paid the last installment of contract funds. According to the contract, the conditions for KeHuixin Company to deliver the intellectual property rights had not yet been satisfied, but it is also necessary to examine whether, due to KeHuixin Company's improper delivery or other conduct, the conditions for Paierte Company's counter-performance obligation to pay the last installment were not satisfied.

Regarding the acceptance standard for the design documents, the parties have a dispute. Paierte Company argues that the contract attachments should prevail, while KeHuixin Company argues that the attachments are the development basis and the delivery content of the design documents should be based on Article 2 of the contract in question. The contract in question is a technology commissioned development contract. Pursuant to Article 332 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the research and developer in a commissioned development contract shall complete the research and development work on schedule in accordance with the agreement, deliver the research and development results, provide relevant technical materials and necessary technical guidance, and help the commissioning party master the research and development results. It can be seen that in a technology commissioned development contract, the commissioning party's contractual purpose is to master the development results. When providing technical materials, the commissioning party shall do so in accordance with the contract and in a manner conducive to achieving the contractual purpose of enabling the commissioning party to master the development results. At the same time, if the development contract stipulates that the commissioning party shall obtain the intellectual property rights of the development results, the commissioned party shall also deliver the relevant technical materials.

The contract in question stipulates that KeHuixin Company is responsible for the development of the electronic control part, and that the relevant intellectual property rights shall be enjoyed by Paierte Company after the development fees are settled in full. In order to achieve the contractual content of obtaining the intellectual property rights of the development results and to realize the contractual purpose of mastering the development results, Paierte Company has a reasonable expectation that KeHuixin Company will deliver the source code for the electronic control part and other relevant materials for the development results, and KeHuixin Company should also cooperate in delivering the corresponding materials when the conditions are met. In addition to the design documents agreed in the contract, delivering the source code and code annotations listed in the "output products and documents" column is also a natural implication of achieving the above contractual purpose. In its reply letter, KeHuixin Company's response to Paierte Company's request to deliver the source code was "the contract does not have this excessive request," and during the second instance, it clearly stated that the list in the contract attachments was not the list of materials to be delivered agreed by the parties, and KeHuixin Company only needed to deliver embedded software, not the source code. The above statement is not only inconsistent with the contract, but also clearly indicates by its own conduct that it will not perform its obligations. Therefore, this Court determines that KeHuixin Company's delivery of materials does not conform to the contract. Accordingly, although the conditions for KeHuixin Company to deliver the intellectual property rights of the development results to Paierte Company have not been satisfied, the failure of Paierte Company to pay the last contract installment was caused by KeHuixin Company's improper delivery. The failure of the conditions does not prevent Paierte Company from demanding, in litigation, that KeHuixin Company transfer to it the patent application right in question in accordance with the contract.

Given that KeHuixin Company's delivery of design documents did not comply with the contract, the payment conditions were not yet satisfied when it sent the reply letter, and Paierte Company's non-payment did not constitute a breach of contract. Therefore, the notice of termination sent by KeHuixin Company cannot have the legal effect of terminating the contract. The court of first instance found that the contract in question had been terminated upon the delivery of KeHuixin Company's notice of termination, which is an improper determination, and this Court hereby corrects it.

4. How to address the ownership of the patent application right in question

Paierte Company requested in the first instance that the ownership of the patent application right in question be confirmed. During the second instance, it indicated that since the patent in question was applied for by KeHuixin Company, its request for confirmation of the application right also includes a request for the court to order KeHuixin Company to transfer the patent application right in question to it. According to the contract, the above request of Paierte Company is subject to the condition that it pays the last installment. The purpose of entering into a contract is primarily to ensure that both parties perform the contract in accordance with the agreement. In a dispute over a bilateral contract, both parties owe mutual counter-performance obligations. Where one party requests the other party to perform its obligations, but due to the other party's breach of contract or other legitimate reasons, it has not actually performed its own counter-performance obligation, the people's court should not simply reject the requesting party's claim solely on the ground that it has not performed its counter-performance obligation. Instead, depending on the specific circumstances of the case, the court may order both parties to perform mutual counter-performance obligations, in order to achieve the purpose of the contract and facilitate a one-time resolution of the dispute. In particular, where the requesting party is willing to perform its own counter-performance obligation, but due to the other party's refusal to accept performance or other breach of contract, the requesting party has a legitimate reason for not actually performing, the people's court may order the other party to perform its performance obligation, while also ordering the requesting party to correspondingly perform its own counter-performance obligation.

In this case, KeHuixin Company improperly delivered first. Paierte Company could exercise its right of defense based on this and not perform the subsequent payment obligation. Paierte Company itself had a legitimate reason for not paying the balance. Moreover, Paierte Company agreed to pay the balance, but its actual performance during the second instance failed because KeHuixin Company refused to accept it. This situation constitutes KeHuixin Company improperly preventing the condition for Paierte Company's request from being satisfied, and it should be deemed that the condition, i.e., the condition for Paierte Company to request the patent application right in question, has been satisfied. Accordingly, Paierte Company's claim for obtaining the patent application right in question should be supported. At the same time, based on the fact that Paierte Company is willing to pay the balance of RMB 15,000, in order to promote the full performance of the contract and resolve the dispute in one instance, the people's court may also require Paierte Company to pay the balance (the last installment of development fees) to KeHuixin Company. Regarding the method of Paierte Company's counter-performance, it may be required that when applying for enforcement of this judgment, Paierte Company pay the counter-performance amount to the enforcement court, to ensure that this counter-performance obligation is also immediately performed after KeHuixin Company's obligation under this judgment is performed. However, given that the amount of Paierte Company's counter-performance is not large, and KeHuixin Company also owes Paierte Company liquidated damages of RMB 6,000, there is no risk in this case that Paierte Company will not perform its counter-performance obligation. Therefore, this Court does not specifically require Paierte Company to pay the amount in advance to the court of first instance. Considering the above factors comprehensively, this Court confirms that the patent application right in question belongs to Paierte Company, and orders that the parties perform counter-performance: KeHuixin Company shall cooperate with Paierte Company in completing the registration of the change of the patent application right, and Paierte Company shall pay KeHuixin Company the balance of the development fees of RMB 15,000.

(B) Regarding the liability for breach of contract claimed by Paierte Company

KeHuixin Company failed to deliver design documents that conform to the contract, and after Paierte Company raised objections, it still refused to deliver, constituting a breach of contract. As for KeHuixin Company's act of applying for the patent in question, since the contract in question stipulates that the intellectual property rights, including the patent application right, belong to KeHuixin Company before the development fees are fully settled, KeHuixin Company's application for the patent in question on December 5, 2018, during the performance of the contract, did not violate the above agreement and does not constitute a breach of contract.

According to the contract, the upper limit of liquidated damages for KeHuixin Company's breach of the obligation to deliver design documents is 10% of the paid amount. Paierte Company has paid a total of RMB 60,000 in contract funds. Therefore, KeHuixin Company shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 6,000 for the improper delivery of design documents. As for the sample production costs claimed by Paierte Company, since it cannot be determined that they are related to the subject matter of the contract in question, and KeHuixin Company does not recognize them, this Court does not support this claim. The contract in question does not stipulate that liability for breach of contract includes bearing the expenses for realizing the claim. Paierte Company's request for KeHuixin Company to compensate for attorney fees and notarization fees lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, part of Paierte Company's appeal claims are established and should be supported. The court of first instance erred in factual findings and application of law, and the judgment should be amended. Pursuant to Articles 107, 332, and 339(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 177(1)(ii) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court orders as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2019) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1716 of the Beijing Intellectual Property Court is set aside;

2. It is confirmed that the right to apply for the invention patent with application number 201811480727.9 and title "A Surgical Stapler and Control Method Thereof" belongs to Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, Shenzhen KeHuixin Technology Co., Ltd. shall cooperate with Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. in completing the registration of the transfer of the patent application right, and Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. shall pay Shenzhen KeHuixin Technology Co., Ltd. development fees of RMB 15,000;

3. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, Shenzhen KeHuixin Technology Co., Ltd. shall pay Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. liquidated damages of RMB 6,000;

4. The other claims of Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be paid doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; if other obligations are not performed within the period specified in this judgment, a charge for delayed performance shall be paid in accordance with the above provision.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 2,662 shall be borne by Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,000, and by Shenzhen KeHuixin Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,662. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 2,662 shall be borne by Beijing Paierte Medical Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,000, and by Shenzhen KeHuixin Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,662.

This judgment is final.
